clue.text: Hoping to see induction of current in a metal coil

indicators.note: an induction is a putting in, so the current is introduced into the coil

parts.note: a spring is a coil of metal
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A physics student hopes to observe a current induced in a coil of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'induction of' puts I inside A SPRING; 'in' simply links.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspiring and hoping are synonyms: both describe wanting to achieve something.

clue.text: Stammering severely, had a gloss for language

indicators.note: a bad stammer repeats the start of a word before getting it out, so a clipped start comes first

parts.note: something that had a gloss shone
shone again, the word finally said in full

explanation.surface: Someone stammering badly had a gloss written for their language.
explanation.walkthrough: A bad stammer stumbles over the start of a word before saying it whole, which is what the clue copies.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoshone is a Native American language of the western United States.

clue.text: I am spreading gums with lotion but my specialty is natural resistance

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm

indicators.note: spreading things out disturbs their order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone smears ointment on their gums while declaring their real expertise is in the body's defences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges IM (I'm, from 'I am') with GUMS and LOTION; 'with' and 'but' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural resistance to disease is immunity, the specialty of a scientist who studies the immune system.

clue.text: Knits woven with a place for quills etc

indicators.note: woven threads are interlaced, so the letters of knits are rearranged

parts.note: and means together with

explanation.surface: Knitting woven together with a spot to keep quill pens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' rearranges KNITS into INKST.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkstand is a stand holding ink and pens such as quills on a desk.

clue.text: Such flesh isn't seen as prime time cuts what's disgusting

definitions.text: Such flesh isn't seen as prime

indicators.note: the time letter cuts into the other word, sitting within it

parts.note: grisly means gruesome or disgusting

explanation.surface: A butcher remarks that poor-quality meat at a peak hour sells cuts that are revolting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' puts T inside GRISLY. 'prime time' and 'cuts' pose as butchery and broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Gristly meat is full of tough cartilage, so nobody would call it prime.

clue.text: Cases of abusiveness provoke court appearance

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so the first and last letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: Instances of abuse lead to someone appearing in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases of' takes the first and last letters of 'abusiveness' (AS) and 'provoke' (PE).
explanation.definitionFit: Aspect means the look or appearance of something.

clue.text: Area of sand trap is halved

parts.note: trap and gob are both slang for the mouth

indicators.note: only half of the word is is kept, its first letter

explanation.surface: A bunker on a golf course is cut in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sand trap' suggests a golf bunker, but 'trap' is slang for the mouth (GOB); half of 'is' gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a vast desert in Mongolia and China, a great expanse of sand.

clue.text: What's designed for draining pressure on ear

parts.note: lughole is British slang for the ear

explanation.surface: Something meant to relieve pressure building up in the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' links, putting P on top of LUGHOLE; LUGHOLE is British slang for an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A plughole is the hole in a sink or bath through which water drains away.

clue.text: Spooner's account of lover's part: it takes cut flowers

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words have their starts exchanged

parts.note: a beau is a lover, so lover's gives beau's
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A Spoonerism about a lover's role, then an unrelated remark about a vase taking flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAU'S ROLE with its B and R sounds swapped becomes ROSE BOLE, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose bowl is a wide bowl for displaying cut flowers.

clue.text: Where keepers preserve life, initially Moses is to go by rushes

parts.note: a zoo is where keepers look after and conserve animal life

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word Moses is wanted

explanation.surface: A Biblical scene of baby Moses among the bulrushes, recast as conservation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rushes' recalls Moses in the bulrushes, but here it means moves in fast bursts.
explanation.definitionFit: To zoom is to move very quickly, rushing past.

clue.text: Perhaps in need of a clue using puns etc in a jumble

definitions.text: Perhaps in need of a clue

indicators.note: things in a jumble are mixed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solver confused by a clue that jumbles puns and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a jumble' rearranges USING PUNS ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unsuspecting is clueless, so perhaps in need of a clue about what is happening.

clue.text: Hollywood actor embracing new extra with new openness

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: Spencer Tracy was a Hollywood film star
N again for new
spare means extra
N again for new

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star hugs a new film extra in a candid way.
explanation.walkthrough: Spencer Tracy was a leading Hollywood star of the 1930s to 1960s; 'with' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Transparency is openness, being frank with nothing hidden.

clue.text: Miró, for example, mostly coats work in this plant oil

indicators.note: one piece covers the other, holding it inside
most of the name is kept, losing its last letter

parts.note: Joan Miró was a Spanish painter, so his first name is Joan
a job is work

explanation.surface: A painter's work is mostly coated in a plant oil.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR lost the accent: the clue names Joan Miró, the Spanish painter, whose first name minus its tail is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Jojoba oil is pressed from the seeds of a desert shrub.

clue.text: Heartbreaker one's extricated from hair, bathed in endless cleanser, say

indicators.note: one piece sits immersed within the other
the last letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a lotion is an example of a cleanser

indicators.note: the letter is pulled out of the word hair

parts.note: one gives I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A womaniser washes his hair in cleanser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartbreaker' is the definition at the front; the rest is a container of a trimmed cleanser round a trimmed hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a seducer who breaks women's hearts, named after a rake in an old play.

clue.text: Two functions restricting leg's lower part

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the leg piece is held between them

parts.note: sec, short for secant, is a mathematical function
a do is a function in the sense of a party
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: Two mathematical functions restrict the lower part of a leg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'functions' is used in two senses, maths and parties. In cricket the on side is the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Secondo is the lower part in a piano duet, the bass part played by the second pianist.

clue.text: Chemical added to raised skin

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: plus means added to
a hide is an animal's skin

explanation.surface: A chemical is applied to an inflamed patch of skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns PLUS into SULP.
explanation.definitionFit: A sulphide is a chemical compound of sulphur with another element.

clue.text: Fashion designer with lines captivating Milan team's foremost pair

indicators.note: captivating suggests holding captive, so the team letters sit inside

parts.note: verse is lines of poetry
the football team AC Milan begins with the letters AC

explanation.surface: A fashion designer writes poetry enchanting the best two players in a Milan football side.
explanation.walkthrough: AC Milan is a famous Italian football club; 'with' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Gianni Versace was an Italian fashion designer whose label still bears his name.

clue.text: Will manager see former partner finally lose share of proceeds otherwise?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word lose is taken

parts.note: a cut is a share of the takings
or means otherwise, as in do it or else

explanation.surface: Will a manager find an ex finally losing their portion of the money?
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' links; 'Will' is the legal document, not the future tense.
explanation.definitionFit: An executor is the person appointed to carry out the instructions of a will.

clue.text: Pencil letters and round figures in vessel's ledger

indicators.note: these pieces are placed inside the vessel word

parts.note: a cask is a barrel, a kind of vessel
HB is the hardness grading printed on pencils
two noughts are round figures

explanation.surface: Someone pencils letters and round numbers into a ship's accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship but is a barrel here; HB is the grade printed on ordinary pencils.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash book is a ledger recording money received and paid out.

clue.text: A man will act crazy for a she-devil

parts.note: a man will contracts to he'll

indicators.note: crazy means wild or deranged, so the letters of act are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man will behave madly for a fiendish woman.
explanation.walkthrough: HE'LL comes from 'A man will'; 'crazy' turns ACT into CAT; 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hellcat is a spiteful, fierce woman, a she-devil.

clue.text: Poles' approach increases such freedom

definitions.meaning: the angular distance from the equator grows as one nears the North or South Pole
scope or leeway to act as one likes

explanation.surface: Getting nearer the poles brings more liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' is the Earth's poles, not people from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is leeway, freedom of action; it is also the geographical measure that rises towards the poles.

clue.text: Clear relation, suppressing the ending, uplifted work

indicators.note: the last letter of the relative is held back

parts.note: an uncle is a relation

indicators.note: in a down entry uplifted means read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: go means work, as in the machine won't go

explanation.surface: A relative, holding back the conclusion, lifted a piece of work clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing the ending' cuts UNCLE to UNCL; 'uplifted' turns GO into OG.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclog a pipe is to clear it of a blockage.

clue.text: Pass further around a piano

indicators.note: the first piece goes around the others

parts.note: else means further or besides
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Someone passes a piano further along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts A and P inside ELSE.
explanation.definitionFit: When time elapses it passes.

clue.text: Unravelling truth or lie involves copper looking after grasses etc

indicators.note: involves means takes in, so the metal letters go inside
something unravelling comes apart, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer is caught up when the truth or a lie comes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the metal's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Horticulture is the cultivation of gardens, tending grasses, plants and flowers.

clue.text: Centrepiece is taken from important upcoming range

indicators.note: the middle letter is removed
in a down entry upcoming means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: major means important

explanation.surface: The centrepiece is removed from an important forthcoming exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' turns MAJOR into ROJAM, and 'Centrepiece is taken from' removes its middle J.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to wander or range freely.

clue.text: Gas weight overlooked by scientist

indicators.note: the weight letters are left out of the scientist's name

parts.note: Isaac Newton was a scientist

explanation.surface: A scientist neglects the weight of a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooked by' takes WT out of NEWTON. Newton, of gravity fame, suits a clue about weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a noble gas used in glowing advertising signs.

clue.text: Arabic work reputed to back people's movement

indicators.note: the whole sequence is read in reverse

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
said means reputed, as in the said person

explanation.surface: An Arabic text reportedly supports a popular campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' reverses AR + OP + SAID, giving DIAS + PO + RA.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is the dispersal of a people from their homeland.

clue.text: Turning, I soak Oriental beef with one?

definitions.text: Turning, I soak Oriental beef with one?

indicators.note: turning round means reversing, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: to ret is to soak flax or hemp
the yak is an Asian ox, a source of beef
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A cook marinates Asian beef in a sauce while turning it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reverses I + RET to give TERI. Read as a whole, the clue describes the marinade.
explanation.definitionFit: Teriyaki is a Japanese glaze in which beef or other meat is marinated and grilled.
